competitive_landscape: A mature commuter-ferry network (Auckland Transport / Fullers360) plus growing Waiheke tourism. The upgrade case is speed, ride quality and emissions in a marine park; no foiling incumbent.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the Auckland harbour mesh and the inner Hauraki Gulf — Waiheke, Devonport, Rangitoto, Tiritiri and (edge) Great Barrier Island.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) could open longer NZ coastal trunks (e.g. Auckland↔Bay of Islands, ~110 nm) as scheduled line-haul.

precedents.why_it_matters: Auckland pairs a managed commuter harbour with an island-rich gulf — both a public-transport upgrade and an island-hopping play in one market.

regulatory_note: New Zealand flag; Maritime NZ certification; Auckland Transport concessions for any public-network integration; Hauraki Gulf Marine Park rules (DOC) favour low-impact operation.
seasonality: Year-round operable; peak NZ summer (Dec–Mar); gulf generally sheltered; occasional winter swells.
summary: Auckland combines a heavy daily ferry-commute market (Devonport, Half Moon Bay, Hobsonville) with the Hauraki Gulf, a marine park studded with islands: Waiheke (wine + lifestyle commuter island), Rangitoto, Tiritiri Matangi and, on the Pioneer edge, Great Barrier Island. The Auckland↔Waiheke run alone is a large, growing commuter-and-tourism corridor. Nearly all legs are inside Pioneer II range, and the marine-park setting rewards a quiet, low-wake foiler. Strong on both public-transport upgrade and island-hopping.
tagline: New Zealand's City of Sails — a busy commuter-ferry harbour fronting the island-rich Hauraki Gulf.
